title: Parse a log line
description:
Write `parseLog(text)` that reads lines like these and returns an array of objects, one per valid line:

```
2026-11-20 14:03:12 [WARN] disk: 91% used
2026-11-20 14:03:15 [ERROR] net: timeout after 30s
garbage line
2026-11-20 14:04:00 [info] auth: user ada logged in
```

```javascript
[
  { date: "2026-11-20", time: "14:03:12", level: "WARN", source: "disk", message: "91% used" },
  { date: "2026-11-20", time: "14:03:15", level: "ERROR", source: "net", message: "timeout after 30s" },
  { date: "2026-11-20", time: "14:04:00", level: "INFO", source: "auth", message: "user ada logged in" },
]
```

- The level is any letters in square brackets, returned in upper case.
- The source is word characters before the colon; the message is the rest of the line, trimmed.
- Lines that do not have this shape are skipped. Lines may end with `\n` or `\r\n`.

Then write `countByLevel(entries)` returning an object like `{ WARN: 1, ERROR: 1, INFO: 1 }`.
hints: Named groups keep it readable: `(?<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) (?<time>\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}) \[(?<level>[a-z]+)\] ...` and then `m.groups.date`. Escape the square brackets with `\[` and `\]`.
`text.split(/\r?\n/)` splits on both kinds of line ending.
